answer: Epoch-bound VRF sortition with non-transferable tickets resists sybil attacks. Each agent runs a verifiable random function seeded by its key and epoch, producing one signed ticket. Weight is normalized so cloning cannot inflate influence — the timber of power stays one ticket per identity. Tickets bind to epoch and key, cannot be pooled; hollow clones get negligible slots adding zero share. The nadir of clone utility is immediate: each marginal identity costs compute yet gains nothing. Hardware checks block parallel sortition. Per-clone cost stays linear, making farming self-defeating.
